messages:
mike: hitting a truststore/SSL headache with the python async SDK when running inside our corp network (HTTPS proxy doing TLS intercept). sync client + raw httpx behave, but AsyncClient wrapper fails on pooled connections.

emily: any stack trace? sounds like a cert chain / context reuse bug.

mike: `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed` from httpcore during connection reuse. first request sometimes OK, subsequent requests fail. we set HTTPS_PROXY and SSL_CERT_FILE to /etc/pki/corp-ca.pem.

kevin: quick suspicion: AsyncClient wrapper builds its own ssl.SSLContext using certifi and `trust_env=False` by default. that means it won't pick up SSL_CERT_FILE or HTTPS_PROXY unless explicitly handled. pooled connections could be reusing a context that never loaded the proxy CA.

emily: exact repro snippet?

mike: minimal: ```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="x", base_url="https://redwood.dedicated.internal")
# env: HTTPS_PROXY=https://corp-proxy:443, SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/pki/corp-ca.pem
await client.generate("hello")
```
works sometimes, then next request fails with cert verify. raw httpx: `httpx.AsyncClient(verify='/etc/pki/corp-ca.pem', trust_env=True, proxies={'https': 'https://corp-proxy:443'})` is rock solid.

kevin: agreed bug summary: async path lacks parity with sync re: `ca_bundle` and `trust_env` handling and constructs SSLContext from certifi only. proposed fixes: (1) add `ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, Path]]` and `trust_env: Optional[bool]` params to AsyncClient constructor, (2) honor SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env when ca_bundle not provided, (3) when trust_env is True and proxies env present, forward proxies to httpx transport, (4) ensure SSLContexts are cached per-verify-path so pooled reuse is safe.

emily: also: disable retry on SSL verification errors by default. current retry layer retries transport-level failures and that just masks a root cert issue and floods logs. `retry_on_ssl=False` default seems right. document how to opt in if someone wants retries for transient proxy resets.

mike: typing friction: mypy errors when trying to pass `verify` through kwargs because AsyncClient signature is narrow. can we add explicit type hints for these params so IDEs show them?

kevin: yes. add explicit typed args in our public constructor and update stubs so `ca_bundle: Optional[Union[str, Path]]`, `trust_env: Optional[bool]`, and `proxies: Optional[Mapping[str,str]]` appear. avoid `**kwargs` catchall to keep DX good. add overloads for advanced httpx transport injection.

emily: small docs ask: add a dedicated troubleshooting section with examples for systemd and k8s, and the httpx one-liner for quick verification: ```bash
# verify CA chain quickly
export HTTPS_PROXY=https://corp-proxy.internal:443
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/pki/corp-ca.pem
python - <<'PY'
import httpx
print(httpx.get('https://redwood.dedicated.internal', verify='/etc/pki/corp-ca.pem').status_code)
PY
```

kevin: i'll open a small additive API PR (no breaking changes) with unit tests: precedence test (explicit ca_bundle > env > certifi), proxy+trust_env integration test using a mocked httpx transport, and a retry test asserting SSLCertVerificationError is non-retriable by default. i'll also add mypy tests to the CI matrix.

ci-bot: opened issue #5788: "py-sdk: async client truststore+proxy parity, trust_env, typing, and ssl-retry defaults" and linked this thread.

mike: thanks 44d that plan sounds good. temporary workaround for folks: create a raw httpx.AsyncClient with `verify` and `trust_env=True` and pass it into the SDK internals, or set REDWOOD_API_BASE_URL to the non-proxied endpoint if possible.

kevin: will ping this thread when the draft PR is ready for review. also will add a changelog note and a short README example for Dedicated customers behind corp proxies.

emily: perfect. once PR lands we'll ask a couple customers to smoke test in corp environments.
